questions.questionText: A care plan for a person who has experienced repeated episodes focuses on preserving functioning while reducing the severity and duration of future episodes. Which combination best classifies this plan?
A patient gives brief answers and describes events out of sequence. Which interviewing approach best supports both therapeutic communication and a comprehensive mental status assessment?
options: Ask a series of specific questions and focus only on the patient’s stated symptoms.
Redirect the patient quickly to factual details while minimizing pauses in the conversation.
Use broad open-ended questions, therapeutic silence, and clarification while observing verbal and nonverbal behavior.
questions.correctAnswer: Use broad open-ended questions, therapeutic silence, and clarification while observing verbal and nonverbal behavior.

options: WHY is a judgment discussion and intrusive. Avoid WHY questions.
questions.correctAnswer: WHY is a judgment discussion and intrusive. Avoid WHY questions.

questions.questionText: A patient appears uncertain about a personal decision and says, “I do not know what to do.” Which response best supports a professional therapeutic relationship?
options: Why are you having difficulty making this decision?
It sounds like you feel uncertain; tell me more about what concerns you.
You should choose the option that seems safest to you.
questions.correctAnswer: It sounds like you feel uncertain; tell me more about what concerns you.

questions.questionText: A patient is preparing to end a therapeutic relationship after practicing adaptive behaviors. Which nursing action best supports this transition?
options: Summarize achieved goals and discuss incorporating newly learned coping strategies
Gather additional objective data and promote problem-solving skills
Address resistant behaviors and redefine problems and goals
Maintain the relationship while facilitating further behavioral change
questions.correctAnswer: Summarize achieved goals and discuss incorporating newly learned coping strategies
